cards.text: Micah, a prophet of the LORD, has a message, and he aims it right at the top. The prophet says, 'Hear now, O leaders of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel.' Then he asks them a question.

cards.question: Micah asks the leaders of Jacob, the people in charge of judging, a question. Of all people, shouldn't they know ___?
The leaders of Jacob should know justice. Micah says they love good and hate evil.

cards.text: Nope, flip it. Micah says they hate good and love evil, and they tear the skin from his people and strip the flesh from their bones.

cards.question: Micah keeps that rough picture going. He says the leaders of Jacob chop up his people like what?

cards.text: Then Micah says a time is coming when these same leaders will cry out to the LORD.

cards.question: The leaders of Jacob cry out to the LORD. What happens?

answers.text: He sends them a new king

cards.question: Micah says the LORD will hide His face from these leaders because of the evil they have done.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks about the prophets who lead His people astray. These prophets proclaim peace while they chew with their teeth.

cards.question: These prophets proclaim peace while they chew. But against someone who puts nothing in their mouths, they declare ___.

cards.text: So their message depends on whether you feed them. That's like me telling you your cookies look PERFECT only after you slip me one, and baker, I'm not saying I've never been tempted.
So the LORD says night will come over these prophets without visions, and the daylight will turn black over them. Signal from heaven? ZERO bars.

cards.question: Once the visions are gone, the seers and diviners are honored for their honesty.
The seers and diviners all end up covering their mouths. Why?

answers.text: There is no answer from God
The leaders ordered them to be quiet
They are afraid of the angry crowds

cards.text: Then the prophet Micah says, 'As for me, however,' and the whole tone changes. Those prophets got no answer from God, but Micah has something they don't.

cards.question: Micah says he is filled with power by the ___ of the LORD.

cards.text: Those prophets went dark, but Micah's running on power the dead batteries I shared that drawer with could only DREAM about. And those batteries swore, SWORE, they still had a little left.

cards.question: Micah is filled with power, justice and courage. What does he declare to Jacob and Israel?

cards.text: Then Micah calls out the leaders of Jacob and rulers of Israel again. He says they despise justice and pervert all that is right.

cards.question: Micah says these leaders build Zion with ___ and Jerusalem with iniquity.

cards.text: Then Micah goes down the list, and it's price tags all the way down. Jerusalem's leaders judge for a bribe, and her prophets practice divination for money.

cards.question: In Jerusalem, Micah says, the priests are the ones who teach for free.
Bribes and price tags all over Jerusalem, and yet they lean on the LORD. What do they say?

answers.text: The LORD is among us so no disaster can come
The LORD has left us so we should repent now
The LORD is angry so we must hide from Him

cards.text: All that, and they still say no disaster can come? That's me hearing the smoke alarm and going, 'Relax, it can't be MY cookies, I'm the BAKER.'
Then Micah says what's coming because of them, and he starts with Zion.

cards.question: Because of Jerusalem's leaders, priests and prophets, what will happen to Zion?

answers.text: It will be plowed like a field
It will be rebuilt with gold
It will be ruled by Egypt

cards.question: Micah says that even if Jerusalem falls, the temple mount will be left standing.

cards.text: Jerusalem becomes a heap of rubble, and the temple mount a wooded ridge. That's where Micah's warning lands, friend, and it does not land soft.

findings.problem: The question calls the leaders of Jacob 'the people in charge of judging.' Micah 3:1 calls them only leaders of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel. Judging comes from 3:11, and pulling it in here also hints at the answer 'justice.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Micah 3:2 says 'my people,' but the card says Micah's 'his people.' Micah may be speaking of God's people, and the text leaves that open. Card 5 has the same problem.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says the leaders 'chop up his people.' Micah 3:3 says 'my people,' and the text leaves open whose people they are.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card tells no new part of the passage. It restates the answer to card 10 and adds a joke, so it works as a recap card holding a joke instead of a joke riding along on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card uses Micah 3:7 ('Those prophets got no answer from God') but cites only Micah 3:8. It should cite Micah 3:7-8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card tells no new part of the passage. It repeats that Micah is filled with power (the answer to card 2) and that the prophets went dark, then adds the battery joke. It is a recap card holding a joke.
'Those prophets went dark' uses Micah 3:6, but the card cites only Micah 3:8. The citation should run from the first verse used to the last.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card tells no new part of the passage. It repeats the answer to card 9 ('they still say no disaster can come') and adds the smoke alarm joke, so it works as a recap card.

The question says Zion falls 'because of Jerusalem's leaders, priests and prophets.' Micah 3:12 says 'because of you,' and in 3:9 Micah addresses the leaders of the house of Jacob and the rulers of the house of Israel. The priests and prophets are described in the third person in 3:11, so the card decides who 'you' is when the text doesn't.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The statement 'the temple mount will be left standing' is meant to be false, but a baker could argue it's true. In Micah 3:12 the temple mount is still there as a wooded ridge, so the hill itself is left. The statement should say clearly what is being claimed, such as the temple mount being spared.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
